correctness.rationale: The exact constraints on terminal-pair shortest paths in a biclique split all edges into four independently selectable blocks. The product counts each feasible edge set once, all minimal solutions are blockwise minima, and the nonnegative-gap identity proves the sharp star/nonstar equality criterion for every 0≤x≤a, 0≤y≤b, x+y≥2. All roots are zero or negative integers from the linear factors. Independent BFS-based direct deletion enumeration on 92 profiles gives exactly the predicted polynomials; finite corroboration is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The general lower-bound source explicitly calls equality-case and minimum-set characterization natural further problems. This theorem resolves both on all complete bipartite graphs and all terminal distributions, giving the full all-set polynomial, a real-rooted coefficient law, complete minimum census, pure inclusion-minimal family, and connected optimum exchange. It shows equality is rigid: only opposing terminal pairs for non-star bicliques, versus every terminal placement for stars. These natural complete-family invariants are not a simple restatement of the general lower bound.
